questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Partition of Bengal:
1. It was announced in July 1905 and took effect on 16 October 1905.
2. It created a new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam with Dacca as its capital.
3. It was carried out by Lord Minto.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Curzon, the Viceroy, carried out the Partition, citing administrative convenience, and Minto succeeded him only in November 1905. The real aim, as the Swadeshi leaders saw it, was to weaken Bengali nationalism by dividing Hindus and Muslims.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, Ch 6; Spectrum, Modern India

questions.q: The province of Bihar and Orissa was created out of the Bengal Presidency in which year, following the annulment of the Partition of Bengal?
questions.e: The King-Emperor announced the annulment at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911 and the shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi. Bihar and Orissa were carved out as a separate province in 1912, and Assam was made a separate province again.
questions.s: Spectrum, Modern India; Bipan Chandra, Ch 6

questions.q: The formal proclamation of the boycott of British goods during the Swadeshi Movement was made on 7 August 1905 at
questions.e: The meeting at Calcutta Town Hall adopted the boycott resolution, and the Partition took effect on 16 October. The Benares Congress of December 1905 only endorsed the Bengal boycott and Swadeshi movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 16 October 1905, the day the Partition of Bengal came into force:
1. It was observed as a day of mourning, with Rakhi tying as a symbol of unity of the Bengalis.
2. Rabindranath Tagore composed 'Amar Sonar Bangla' for the movement.
3. The foundation stone of the Federation Hall was laid by Surendranath Banerjea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Federation Hall foundation, symbolising Bengal's unity, was laid by Ananda Mohan Bose. Tagore's song became a national anthem of Bangladesh decades later.

questions.q: The Carlyle Circular of 1905 was issued by the Bengal Government to
o: stop the import of British cloth into Bengal
ban the use of the song Vande Mataram in public
prevent students from taking part in the Swadeshi and boycott agitation
questions.e: It threatened to withdraw grants and affiliation from schools and colleges whose students took part in political agitation. Students formed the Anti-Circular Society in reply, and the controversy led to the national education movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Council of Education (1906):
1. It was set up in Bengal to organise a system of national education run by Indians.
2. Aurobindo Ghosh became the first principal of the Bengal National College.
3. Rabindranath Tagore was its first principal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Council was a response to the Carlyle Circular and to the demand for education on national lines, which formed one of the four planks of the Extremist programme. Tagore supported the movement but was not the principal.
questions.s: Spectrum, Modern India; Bipan Chandra, Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company — V.O. Chidambaram Pillai
2. Bengal Chemical and Pharmaceutical Works — P.C. Ray
3. Swadeshi Bandhab Samiti, Barisal — Ashwini Kumar Dutt
4. Dawn Society — Surendranath Banerjea
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Dawn Society was founded by Satish Chandra Mukherjee (1902), not by Surendranath Banerjea.

questions.q: Who led the Swadeshi Movement in Delhi?
questions.e: Outside Bengal the movement was led by Tilak (Maharashtra), Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh (Punjab), Chidambaram Pillai (Madras) and Haider Raza (Delhi). This spread showed how the idea of Swadeshi had gone beyond Bengal.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Many Muslim landlords and elites of East Bengal supported the Partition of Bengal.
Statement-II: The Partition created a Muslim-majority province with Dacca as its capital, promising them better educational and employment opportunities.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Nawab of Dacca, Salimullah, who received a government loan, backed the Partition. Their expectations explain this stand, and the British used the division to widen the Hindu-Muslim gap.

questions.q: The police attacked the Provincial Conference at Barisal in April 1906 for the use of 'Bande Mataram' slogans. Who presided over the Conference?
questions.e: Abdul Rasul, a barrister, presided and the police broke up the conference; Surendranath Banerjea was arrested. The incident turned many Moderates towards sharper protest.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. The Boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
2. The Partition of Bengal coming into effect
3. The Calcutta session of the Congress declaring Swaraj as the goal
4. The Muzaffarpur bomb
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Town Hall boycott resolution (August 1905) came before the Partition took effect (October 1905). The Calcutta Congress of December 1906 followed, and the Muzaffarpur bomb was thrown in April 1908.
questions.h: Aug boycott, Oct partition, Dec Swaraj, Apr bomb.

questions.q: The statement 'Bengal united is a power; Bengal divided will pull in several different ways' occurs in a note on the Partition by
questions.e: Risley, the Home Secretary, argued in 1904 that dividing Bengal would weaken the centre of political agitation. The statement reveals the political motive behind the administrative argument.

questions.q:
Which of the following contributed to the decline of the Swadeshi Movement by 1908?
1. Severe government repression, including laws against meetings and the press
2. The split in the Congress at Surat in 1907
3. The Non-Cooperation Movement led by Gandhi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Arrests of leaders, deportations and the Surat split left the movement without leadership and without mass organisation. The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920, long after.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Swadeshi Movement gave a boost to Indian-owned enterprises like textile mills, soap and match factories.
Statement-II: Many of these Swadeshi ventures failed because of shortage of capital and technical know-how.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true: swadeshi enterprise did grow, but many ventures were short-lived. The second statement does not explain the first; it describes the limits of the revival.

questions.q: The four-fold programme of the Extremists, adopted at the Calcutta session of 1906, consisted of
o: Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott and national education
Swadeshi, boycott, passive resistance and civil disobedience
Self-government, Swadeshi, communal harmony and national education
questions.e: The 1906 resolutions were a compromise under Naoroji's leadership. Swaraj meant self-government on the lines of the United Kingdom or colonies.

questions.q: Which of the following was a revolutionary society set up in Bengal in 1902 by Pramathanath Mitra and Satish Chandra Bose?
questions.e: Anushilan Samiti was the first of the revolutionary groups of the Swadeshi era in Bengal. Jugantar, led by Barindra Ghosh, was an offshoot with its own weekly.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Organisation) with List-II (Leader/Founder):
List-I
A. Abhinav Bharat
B. India House (London)
C. Ghadar Party
D. Hindustan Republican Association
List-II
1. Shyamji Krishna Varma
2. V.D. Savarkar
3. Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
4. Sachindranath Sanyal and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Savarkar led Abhinav Bharat, Shyamji Krishna Varma ran India House and The Indian Sociologist from London, Har Dayal and Bhakna led the Ghadar Party, and Sanyal and Chatterjee founded the HRA in 1924.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Muzaffarpur bomb of 1908:
1. Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw the bomb, meaning to kill the magistrate Kingsford.
2. Two British women, Mrs Kennedy and her daughter, were killed instead.
3. Aurobindo Ghosh was convicted in the Alipore Bomb Case and transported.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Aurobindo was defended by C.R. Das and acquitted; Barindra Ghosh and others were sentenced. Khudiram was hanged, and Chaki shot himself on being cornered.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Curzon Wyllie assassinated in London (1909) — Madan Lal Dhingra
2. A.M.T. Jackson shot at Nashik (1909) — Khudiram Bose
3. Bomb thrown at Lord Hardinge (1912) — Rash Behari Bose
4. Michael O'Dwyer assassinated in London (1940) — Udham Singh
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Jackson was shot at Nashik by Anant Kanhere, in the Nashik conspiracy case; Khudiram was involved in the Muzaffarpur incident of 1908.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ghadar Party:
1. It was founded in 1913 in San Francisco as the Hindustan Association of the Pacific Coast.
2. Sohan Singh Bhakna was its president and Lala Har Dayal its secretary.
3. Lala Har Dayal was its first president.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The party took its name from its weekly Ghadar, and planned an armed uprising in India during the First World War. Har Dayal was the secretary and chief ideologue, not the president.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Komagata Maru passengers, mostly Punjabis, were refused entry at Vancouver in 1914.
Statement-II: Canadian immigration rules required immigrants to arrive by continuous journey from their country of origin, which was impossible from India.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 'continuous journey' rule of 1908 was devised to exclude Indians. The ship, chartered by Baba Gurdit Singh, returned to Calcutta where the police fired at Budge Budge in September 1914.

questions.q: The Provisional Government of India, set up at Kabul in December 1915, had as its President
questions.e: Mahendra Pratap was President, Barkatullah Prime Minister and Obaidullah Sindhi Home Minister, in a plan allied with the Germans and Turks to attack British India. The Silk Letter conspiracy was part of the same effort.

questions.q: Jatindranath Mukherjee, 'Bagha Jatin', who died in a gunfight with the police at Balasore in 1915, was associated with
o: the Indo-German conspiracy, an attempt to obtain German arms for an uprising
questions.e: During the First World War, revolutionaries tried to use German help for an armed rising, with the Jugantar group in Bengal playing a major role. The other events happened in 1930, 1925 and 1929.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA):
1. It was founded at Kanpur in 1924.
2. The Kakori train robbery of 9 August 1925 was carried out by its members.
3. Chandrashekhar Azad was among those hanged for the Kakori conspiracy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in December 1927. Azad escaped arrest and died in 1931 in a police encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The HRA was reorganised in 1928 as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
Statement-II: Under the influence of Bhagat Singh and his comrades, the revolutionaries accepted socialism as their goal.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: At a meeting at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi in September 1928, the group added 'Socialist' to its name. This marked a shift from nationalism alone to a vision of a socialist republic.

questions.q: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and others shot J.P. Saunders, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, at Lahore in December 1928 in order to
o: protest against the Public Safety Bill
avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai
questions.e: Lajpat Rai was injured in a lathi-charge on a Simon Commission demonstration in Lahore and died in November 1928. The shooting was in revenge, though the revolutionaries had intended to hit the Superintendent of Police, Scott.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Legislative Assembly bomb of 8 April 1929:
1. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw the bombs.
2. The bombs were meant to kill members of the Assembly.
3. It was a protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The bombs were deliberately harmless; they aimed 'to make the deaf hear' and the two courted arrest to use the trial to spread their ideas. The leaflets thrown with it announced that purpose.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931.
2. Jatin Das died in Lahore jail in 1929 after a long hunger strike to demand better treatment of political prisoners.
3. The Naujawan Bharat Sabha was founded in 1926 by Bhagat Singh and his comrades.
4. The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' was coined by Bhagat Singh.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The slogan was coined by Hasrat Mohani in 1921 and popularised by Bhagat Singh and his comrades.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revolutionary movement in Chittagong:
1. Surya Sen led the raid on the armoury on 18 April 1930.
2. Pritilata Waddedar led an attack on the Pahartali European Club in 1932.
3. Surya Sen was executed in 1930, soon after the raid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Surya Sen was arrested in 1933 and hanged in January 1934. The raid took place during the Civil Disobedience Movement and women such as Pritilata and Kalpana Dutt took part.

questions.q: The Ghadarites planned an armed uprising in Punjab in February 1915, but it failed. The main reason was that
o: the Indian soldiers in Punjab refused to join in any circumstances
the German government cancelled its support at the last moment
the Congress leaders refused to give permission for the rising
the Government learnt of the plan through an informer and made mass arrests
questions.e: Police infiltration, with an informer inside the group, led to arrests and the Lahore Conspiracy Case; Kartar Singh Sarabha was among those hanged. The Singapore Mutiny of 1915 by the 5th Light Infantry was part of the same wartime wave but also ended in repression.

questions.q: Who unfurled the Indian national flag, as designed by her group, at the International Socialist Congress at Stuttgart in 1907?
questions.e: Madame Cama, a Parsi from Bombay who lived in Paris, represented Indian nationalism abroad and called for independence. She also worked with Savarkar and Shyamji Krishna Varma's circle.
questions.s: Spectrum, Modern India; Bipan Chandra, Ch 7

questions.q:
Shyamji Krishna Varma is associated with which of the following?
1. The Indian Home Rule Society (1905) in London
2. The journal The Indian Sociologist
3. India House in London
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are correct. India House served as a hostel and centre for Indian students in London, with Savarkar, Madan Lal Dhingra and V.V.S. Aiyar among its members.
questions.s: Spectrum, Modern India; Bipan Chandra, Ch 7

questions.q: V.D. Savarkar escaped from custody while being taken to India for trial, by jumping off the ship at
questions.e: He had been arrested in London in 1910 in connection with the Nashik conspiracy and escaped at Marseilles, but was recaptured on the French coast. He was transported to the Cellular Jail in the Andamans in 1911.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Revolutionary Journal) with List-II (Associated Person):
List-I
A. Yugantar
B. Sandhya
C. The Indian Sociologist
D. Ghadar
List-II
1. Brahmabandhab Upadhyay
2. Bhupendranath Dutta and Barindra Ghosh
3. Shyamji Krishna Varma
4. Lala Har Dayal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Bengali weekly Yugantar was run by Barindra Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta (Vivekananda's brother). Sandhya, a Bengali daily, was run by Brahmabandhab Upadhyay, and Ghadar was the Ghadar Party's organ.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. The Muzaffarpur bomb
2. The assassination of Curzon Wyllie by Madan Lal Dhingra
3. The bomb attack on Lord Hardinge at Delhi
4. The founding of the Ghadar Party
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Muzaffarpur bomb was in 1908, the Curzon Wyllie assassination in July 1909, the Delhi attack on Lord Hardinge in December 1912 and the Ghadar Party was formed in 1913.

questions.q: The term 'Satyagraha' was coined by Gandhi after he modified 'Sadagraha', a term suggested in a contest in Indian Opinion by
questions.e: Gandhi felt that 'passive resistance' was an inadequate English term and rejected it; he changed 'Sadagraha' to 'Satyagraha', meaning insistence on truth. Polak and Kallenbach were his European associates in South Africa.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's years in South Africa:
1. He founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.
2. The Phoenix Settlement was set up near Johannesburg.
3. Tolstoy Farm was set up near Johannesburg in 1910.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Phoenix Settlement (1904), inspired by Ruskin's Unto This Last, was near Durban in Natal. Gandhi's weekly Indian Opinion was published from it.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Gandhi's first satyagraha in South Africa began in 1906 against the compulsory registration and fingerprinting of Indians in the Transvaal.
Statement-II: The Transvaal Asiatic Law Amendment Ordinance (the 'Black Act') of 1906 required all Indians to carry registration certificates.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: At a mass meeting in the Empire Theatre, Johannesburg, Indians took a pledge to defy the law. The Ordinance explains why the satyagraha began.

questions.q: The abolition of the £3 poll tax on ex-indentured Indians in South Africa followed
o: the Gandhi-Smuts Agreement of 1914 and the Indian Relief Act
questions.e: The 1913 satyagraha included a march of miners and indentured workers from Newcastle (Natal) into the Transvaal against the tax, and led to the compromise. After this success Gandhi left South Africa in 1914 and returned to India in January 1915.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's return to India:
1. He returned from South Africa in January 1915.
2. On the advice of G.K. Gokhale, he spent a year travelling in India to understand the country before taking a public stand.
3. He set up his first ashram in India at Sabarmati in 1915.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: His first ashram in India was at Kochrab, Ahmedabad (1915); it moved to Sabarmati in 1917. Gokhale's advice, which Gandhi followed, kept him out of politics for a year.

questions.q:
Statement-I: At Champaran in 1917, Gandhi refused an order to leave the district, and the Government withdrew the case against him.
Statement-II: Gandhi had been invited by Rajkumar Shukla to look into the grievances of indigo cultivators.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II explains why Gandhi went to Champaran, not why the Government withdrew its order. The Government gave in because Gandhi was prepared to accept jail, and it appointed an enquiry committee on which Gandhi sat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Champaran Satyagraha:
1. Under the tinkathia system, peasants had to grow indigo on three-twentieths of their land for European planters.
2. It was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India.
3. The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolished the tinkathia system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Act, based on the enquiry committee's recommendation, abolished the tinkathia system and ordered refunds of a part of the illegal dues. Rajendra Prasad, Mazharul Haque and J.B. Kripalani were among Gandhi's helpers.

questions.q: Gandhi's first hunger strike in India was undertaken during the
questions.e: The dispute over the plague bonus led to a strike. When the workers began to waver, Gandhi fasted, and the owners agreed to arbitration, which awarded a 35 percent wage increase. The mill-owner Ambalal Sarabhai's sister Anasuya supported the workers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kheda Satyagraha (1918):
1. Peasants of Kheda demanded remission of land revenue as their crops had failed.
2. Vallabhbhai Patel emerged as a leading organiser.
3. It ended with complete remission of revenue for all peasants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Revenue Code entitled peasants to remission if the yield was below one-fourth of normal. The Government instead issued an instruction that revenue be collected only from those who could pay, a face-saving compromise.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In Hind Swaraj (1909), Gandhi was sharply critical of modern industrial civilisation.
Statement-II: Gandhi held that real swaraj meant self-rule and moral self-control, and that a mere replacement of British rulers by Indians would not achieve it.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in Gujarati on a voyage from London to South Africa in 1909, as a dialogue between an Editor and a Reader. His idea of swaraj as moral self-rule explains his critique of western industrial civilisation.

questions.q: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya', a Gujarati adaptation, was based on which work by John Ruskin that deeply influenced him?
o: The Kingdom of God Is Within You
questions.e: Gandhi read Unto This Last on a train journey in 1904 and set up the Phoenix Settlement to apply its ideas of dignity of labour and the good of all. The Kingdom of God Is Within You is by Tolstoy and Civil Disobedience by Thoreau.

questions.q: Gandhi returned the Kaisar-i-Hind medal, awarded to him for his ambulance corps work in the Boer War, in which year?
questions.e: He surrendered the medal at the start of the Non-Cooperation Movement, in protest against the Punjab wrongs and the Khilafat betrayal. He had organised the Indian Ambulance Corps in 1899-1900.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rowlatt Act (1919):
1. It allowed detention of suspects without trial for up to two years.
2. Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha and called for a nationwide hartal on 6 April 1919.
3. It was passed with the support of all the Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All the Indian members opposed the Bill, and Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazharul Haque resigned from the Council. The hartal movement led to firing in Punjab and ultimately to Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Champaran Satyagraha
2. Ahmedabad mill strike
3. Kheda Satyagraha
4. Rowlatt Satyagraha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Champaran began in 1917, the Ahmedabad strike in February-March 1918, the Kheda movement from March 1918 and the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919. These local struggles gave Gandhi a base before he led a nationwide movement.

questions.q: Gandhi was thrown out of a first-class compartment at Pietermaritzburg station in June 1893 while travelling to
questions.e: He was in South Africa to work on a case for the firm Dada Abdulla and Co. The racial insult started his turn towards public work and his campaign for Indian rights.
